item.title: Non-Amenability of Small Overlap Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.33430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every semigroup admitting a presentation satisfying the small overlap condition $C(3)$ is neither left nor right reversible, unless it is the free semigroup on one generator. Consequently, all such semigroups outside this exception are both left and right non-amenable. We also show the optimality of this result, giving examples of $C(2)$ semigroups that are left and right amenable. Our proof makes use of semigroup diagrams, extending the results of Remmers who first introduced the methods as a means of studying small overlap semigroups. We also compare this to the known result that the $C(7)$ condition in groups implies hyperbolicity which then implies non-amenability (excluding the elementary cases). We establish that, for $m\geq 4$, a strongly $C(m)$ semigroup presentation induces an enveloping group presentation satisfying the small cancellation condition $C(2m-6)$, and show that this bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Margaret Shideler

item.title: Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.
item.dc:creator: Qian Chen, Qiang Zhang, Dongxiao Zhao

item.title: A note on characterization of S4 x C2^n
item.description: arXiv:2611.34180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every non-negative integer n, we characterize S4 x C2^n by its poset of isomorphic classes of subgroups. This provides an infinite family of counterexamples to the conjectures posed by Tarnauceanu in [8] and [9].
item.dc:creator: Tushar Halder, Sachin Ballal

item.title: Normal abelian subgroups of order 5^6 in finite 5-groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite 5-group containing an abelian subgroup of order 5^6 has a normal abelian subgroup of that order. If the given subgroup is elementary abelian, the normal subgroup can be chosen elementary abelian. This resolves n=6, the last open case of both parts of Problem~21.51 of the Kourovka Notebook for p=5. Together with earlier results, it follows that 1\le n\le 6 is the exact range in which each assertion holds for every finite 5-group at subgroup order 5^n. In a minimal counterexample, five conjugate abelian subgroups generate a group of class at most three. In class two we construct invariant isotropic subgroups for the commutator pairing. In class three the Jacobi identity produces a nonzero plane cubic over the field of five elements. The five conjugate subgroups give five distinct singular points spanning the plane, which forces the cubic to vanish.
item.dc:creator: L\"u Gong, Jiaye Chen, Baojun Li

item.title: On some problems regarding a group-theoretical generalization of the Gauss formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.34371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In \cite{FT23}, we introduced the group-theoretical function $f(G) = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{H \le G} |\Aut(H)|$ for a finite group $G$ and posed three open problems concerning its values on noncyclic groups. In this note, we provide complete solutions to all three problems.
item.dc:creator: Marius T\u{a}rn\u{a}uceanu

item.title: Stable finiteness and combination theorems for Hughes-free embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2611.34571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that all group algebras of Higman's group and Deligne's group are stably finite. We also study when the Hughes-free embeddability property is closed under taking graphs of groups, and give a positive answer when the edge maps are retractions or injective on Abelianisations. As a consequence we obtain that fundamental groups of graphs of torsion-free Abelian groups, graph products of locally indicable Hughes-free embeddable groups, and fundamental groups of graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups are Hughes-free embeddable.
item.dc:creator: Sam P. Fisher, Giles Gardam, Pablo S\'anchez-Peralta

item.title: A formula to construct all elements of finite order in Riordan matrix groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the elements of finite order in the Riordan group over the complex field by providing explicit conditions on their entries. Our main result generalizes a previous characterization of involutions to arbitrary finite orders and gives a constructive procedure to determine all Riordan matrices of a prescribed finite order from a suitable choice of parameters. The proof relies on an inductive analysis of the principal submatrices. We further derive consequences for the Lagrange subgroup and the group of formal power series under composition, obtaining a characterization of finite-order series and a constructive description of the solutions to associated functional equations.
item.dc:creator: Irina Ar\'evalo, Ismael G\'omez Garc\'ia, Ana Luz\'on, M. M. Mart\'inez-Rico, L. F. Prieto-Mart\'inez

item.title: Tensor products of finite groups without compatibility conditions are finite
item.description: arXiv:2611.34727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been an open question whether Inassaridze's tensor product $G\otimes H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative, and, as a consequence, we prove that the low dimensional nonabelian homology groups $H_i(G,A)$, $i=0,1$, are finite whenever $G$ and $A$ are finite. We achieve this by introducing a much more general tensor product $G\bt H$, defined for groups acting on themselves and on each other by arbitrary automorphisms, with no compatibility conditions, and subject only to the two defining relations of the nonabelian tensor product. We prove that $G\bt H$ is finite whenever $G$ and $H$ are finite. Since the nonabelian tensor product of Brown and Loday, Inassaridze's tensor product and the box-tensor product are all quotients or special cases of $G\bt H$, this brings the finiteness results for all these tensor products under one umbrella.
item.dc:creator: Sathasivam Kalithasan, Viji Zachariah Thomas

item.title: On the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recall that a class of groups $\mathfrak{F}$ is called $D_\mathfrak{X}$-closed if it contains every group $G = MN$ where $M$ and $N$ are normal $\mathfrak{F}$-subgroups of $G$ and $M\cap N\in \mathfrak{X}$. We prove that a hereditary formation of $\omega$-soluble groups is an $n$-multiply $\omega$-local formation if and only if it is a $D_{\mathfrak{N}^n_\omega}$-closed formation. As corollaries we obtain the theorem of Bryce and Cossey about saturation of hereditary Fitting formations of finite soluble groups and its extension to the class of all $\pi$-soluble groups, as well as the criterion for a formation of soluble groups to be $n$-multiply local.
item.dc:creator: Liudmila V. Ivanova, Viachaslau I. Murashka, Alexander F. Vasil'ev

item.title: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.34793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Houdayer, Basile Morando

item.title: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
item.description: arXiv:2611.34842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.
item.dc:creator: Tianqi Wang

item.title: On Zappa--Sz\'ep products of multiplicative racks
item.description: arXiv:2611.34851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Zappa--Sz\'ep products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Sz\'ep products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Sz\'ep factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Sz\'ep actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Takano

item.title: Extensions of congruent monotileable (and amenable) groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A monotile of a countable group $G$ is a finite subset $F \subseteq G$ that tiles $G$, namely $G=\bigsqcup_{c\in C} c F$, for some set of centers $C\subseteq G$. The group $G$ is called congruent monotileable (CM) if it admits an exhaustive sequence of monotiles $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each $F_{n+1}$ is teselated by $F_n$. If moreover $G$ is amenable and the sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is Folner, we say $G$ is congruent monotileable amenable (CMA). In this work we observe that the classes of CM and CMA groups are stable under group extensions satisfying a certain technical condition, which we call $stepwise$ $monotileability$, and which is a weaker version of the notion of $X$-$monotileability$ introduced by Dikranjan $et al$. Our condition also includes central extensions previously considered by Gao, Jackson, Seward for CM groups, and by Cecchi Bernales, Cortez for CMA groups. We show that this condition is satisfied by semidirect products of the form $G\wr H$, provided $G$ and $H$ are CM/CMA groups, and also by extensions of locally finite groups by CM/CMA groups. This furnishes new examples of CM and CMA groups. In particular, we provide the first examples of finitely generated CMA groups which are neither solvable nor residually finite.
item.dc:creator: Paulina Cecchi-Bernales, Emir Molina, Crist\'obal Rivas

item.title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
item.description: arXiv:2611.33675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.
item.dc:creator: Zhan Ying, Chao-Ping Dong

item.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.34308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $\Gamma$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $\Gamma$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Orzechowski

item.title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
item.description: arXiv:2611.34497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ruhstorfer

item.title: On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.34528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $\sigma\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(\sigma))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(\sigma))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(\sigma)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $\sigma$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Yin Hui, Zhengyu Zhou

item.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincar\'e pairing on $S^3/\Gamma$. In particular, $\Gamma$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.
item.dc:creator: Baizhou Jin, Zichang Wang

item.title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.34787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property. By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.
item.dc:creator: Hannes Kn\"otzele, Sven M\"oller

item.title: Rigidity and flexibility results for groups with a common cocompact envelope
item.description: arXiv:2510.24581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A locally compact group $G$ is a cocompact envelope of a group $\Gamma$ if $G$ contains a copy of $\Gamma$ as a discrete and cocompact subgroup. We study the problem that takes two finitely generated groups $\Gamma,\Lambda$ having a common cocompact envelope, and asks what properties must be shared between $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$. We first consider the setting where the common cocompact envelope is totally disconnected. In that situation we show that if $\Gamma$ admits a finitely generated nilpotent normal subgroup $A$, then virtually $\Lambda$ admits a normal subgroup $B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are virtually isomorphic. We establish both rigidity and flexibility results when $\Gamma$ belongs to the class of solvable groups of finite rank. On the rigidity perspective, we show that if $\Gamma$ is solvable of finite rank, and the locally finite radical of $\Lambda$ is finite, then $\Lambda$ must be virtually solvable of finite rank. On the flexibility perspective, we exhibit groups $\Gamma,\Lambda$ with a common cocompact envelope such that $\Gamma$ is solvable of finite rank, while $\Lambda$ is not virtually solvable. In particular the class of solvable groups of finite rank is not QI-rigid. We also exhibit flexibility behaviours among finitely presented groups, and more generally among groups with type $F_n$ for arbitrary $n \geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Le Boudec

item.title: On the Sum of Element Orders in Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.08320v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\psi(G) = \sum_{g \in G} o(g)$ denote the sum of element orders of a finite group $G$. It is known that among groups of order $n$, the cyclic group $C_n$ maximizes $\psi$. T\u{a}rn\u{a}uceanu proved that two finite abelian $p$-groups of the same order are isomorphic if and only if they have the same sum of element orders, and conjectured this for arbitrary finite abelian groups. In this paper, we confirm the conjecture by proving a stronger result: for finite $LCM$-groups $G$ and $H$ of the same order, $\psi(G) = \psi(H)$ if and only if $G$ and $H$ have the same order type.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Amiri

item.title: A new class of affine $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2512.00318v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a certain class of affine hyperplane arrangements are $K(\pi,1)$ by endowing their Falk complexes with an injective metric. This gives new examples of infinite $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements in dimension $n>2$.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Goldman, Jingyin Huang

item.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2607.25846v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element (and the empty set red). Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, right almost invariant subsets are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed, self-contained account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then give a proof of Protasov's stronger conclusion for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---showing that the full Higson corona is a singleton.
item.dc:creator: Hussain AL-Rasheed

item.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
item.description: arXiv:2611.28382v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\in\gamma_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ cyclic syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of cyclic syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for words with six and eight syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Keren

item.title: Product sets in sets of returns and positivity of symmetric ergodic averages
item.description: arXiv:2608.02873v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study sets of (measurable) returns in countable groups $G$, namely sets of the form $\{g\in G:\mu(A\cap T_gA)>0\}$ arising from measure-preserving actions. Extending a result of Bergelson, we show that sets of returns in $G\times G$ contain subsets of the form $B\times B$, where $B$ is large with respect to suitable notions of largeness that remain meaningful even for non-amenable groups. As a consequence, if $G$ is amenable, then every sufficiently large subset $A\subseteq G\times G$ satisfies $B\times B\subseteq AA^{-1}$ for some large set $B\subseteq G$. We also investigate when sets of returns in $G$ contain product sets $BB$ with $B$ large. In contrast with the Cartesian-product phenomenon above, this problem is considerably subtler in non-abelian groups and is closely connected to `symmetric correlation functions', namely functions of the form $g\mapsto \mu(T_g^{-1}A\cap T_gA)$. We use this connection to show that, for broad classes of amenable groups - including finitely generated nilpotent groups and certain solvable non-nilpotent groups, every sufficiently large set $A\subseteq G$ contains a large subset $B$ satisfying $BB\subseteq AA^{-1}$. Finally, we establish polynomial analogues of these results for finitely generated nilpotent groups, extending earlier work of Bergelson and Ruzsa.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Bergelson, Sa\'ul Rodr\'iguez-Mart\'in

item.title: Vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs in the switching class of doubly transitive two-graphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.30330v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a finite two-graph whose full automorphism group $G$ is $2$-transitive. Up to complementation, we classify the primitive strongly regular graphs with associated two-graph $\mathcal{T}$ whose full automorphism group is a transitive maximal subgroup of $G$ and does not contain the largest perfect subgroup of $G$. In doing so, we obtain a new family of vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs whose associated two-graph arises from $P\Sigma L(2,q)$.
item.dc:creator: Robert F. Bailey, G\'abor P. Nagy, Valentino Smaldore

item.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
item.description: arXiv:2610.17389v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest. We also show that, in an arbitrary semi-abelian category, an extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ is central relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of two-nilpotent objects, defined by means of the ternary Higgins commutator, precisely when the ternary Higgins commutator $[K,A,A]_{\mathsf{Hig}}$ vanishes; a similar characterization holds in the $n$-nilpotent case.
item.dc:creator: Marino Gran, James R. A. Gray, Vito Volpe

item.title: A nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring with finitely based matrix semirings
item.description: arXiv:2611.14551v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish that the matrix semiring $\mathbf{M}_n(SR_6)$ over the six-element nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring $SR_6$ is finitely based for every $n \geq 2$. This provides the first known example of an additively idempotent semiring $S$ that is nonfinitely based, while the matrix semirings $\mathbf{M}_n(S)$ are finitely based. Moreover, we show that the interval $[\mathsf{V}(SR_6), \mathsf{V}(\mathbf{M}_2(SR_6))]$ in the lattice of additively idempotent semiring varieties has the cardinality of the continuum.
item.dc:creator: Jun Jiao, Miaomiao Ren
